title.orig: Sonnet 60: Like as the waves make towards the pebbled shore
title.en: Sonnet 60: Like as the waves make towards the pebbled shore
title.zh: 十四行诗第六十首：像海浪一波波涌向卵石的海岸

edition.en: Text of the 1609 quarto as given by Project Gutenberg (eBook 1041)
edition.zh: 据古登堡计划电子书 1041 所录 1609 年四开本文本

basis.en: Published in 1609 (Shakespeare’s Sonnets, Thomas Thorpe); the author died in 1616.
basis.zh: 1609 年出版（托马斯·索普印行的《莎士比亚十四行诗》）；作者卒于 1616 年。

note.en: A sonnet about time that moves like the thing it describes: the waves of the first line keep arriving, each quatrain pushing the last one out. Shakespeare gives Time a scythe and lets it take almost everything, then turns on a single word, “yet”. It sits here for that turn, from what is lost to what is kept.
note.zh: 一首写时间的十四行诗，它本身就像它所写的东西那样运动：第一行的浪不断涌来，每一节四行都把上一节推出去。莎士比亚给了时间一把镰刀，让它几乎带走一切，然后在一个词上转身——“然而”。它放在这里，是为了那个转折：从失去的，转向被保住的。

excerpt.orig:
And yet to times in hope, my verse shall stand,
Praising thy worth, despite his cruel hand.
excerpt.en:
And yet to times in hope, my verse shall stand,
Praising thy worth, despite his cruel hand.
excerpt.zh:
然而，我的诗将屹立到所期望的未来，
赞美你的美德，不顾他残酷的手。
